role: Character brand director A — personal voice and authorship

recommendation: Test two small cameos as one background workshop interaction. Keep the moth-only image as the comparison and fallback. Do not distribute a full reference cast through the park.
evidence: Viewed assets/brand/banner-park/park-day-study-02-macbook.png with view_image; tool displayed a 2048x683 resize of the 2172x724 image.
Viewed the actual locally attached picnic reference with view_image: /tmp/codex-remote-attachments/01a1b473-8621-7941-ba03-4b47867c136c/D31EE005-F5E8-41CB-97E7-95E073243BDD/1-Photo-1.jpg.
Applied the latest owner constraint supplied by root: absolutely no companion on or near the foreground bench or path; foreground character remains only the moth coding on the MacBook.
observedComposition: The park already has an authored relationship between a large foreground coder, a smaller workshop builder and a resting moth under the tree. They represent the same person in three activities. The curving open path and depth make the composition more than a nameplate. The picnic reference places a bright cast and logo-filled basket in the central focus; importing that arrangement would change the subject from Nag's world to a gathering of other identities.
placementAndStory: Keep both cameos behind the workshop table, on its far side near the canopy or distant tree line. Let the table partly occlude their lower bodies to establish that they are behind the work. Neither may enter the foreground path, bench, coder silhouette or MacBook area.

Give them one shared reason to be there: both notice the same small thing the workshop moth is making, with one curious lean or exchanged reaction. Avoid two unrelated scenes, a spectator semicircle, advertising poses or a row of badges.

Begin around half the workshop moth's visible height or smaller, clearly much smaller than the foreground coder. This is a test range, not a proven pixel specification. Their lighting and material should belong to the park; bright contrasting shapes must not become the first visual stop.

Preserve the resting moth's quiet pocket and the open path. The background visitors are optional discoveries, not the banner's explanation. Keep existing tiny V5 anatomy and Nag's name/voice as the personal identity.
countRationale: Two can suggest company and curiosity while reading as one supporting event. Three would add another face and usually a second action; the existing three moth appearances already provide narrative breadth. The full cast and branded basket would overload the personal story. Zero remains preferable if even two fail the hierarchy test. The specific product roster is not selected, and I do not identify every reference symbol as an AI product.
failureCriteria: Any companion appears on or near the foreground bench/path, or overlaps the foreground moth/MacBook: reject that rendering against the owner's hard constraint.

At actual GitHub banner size, a cameo's shape, saturation or contrast pulls attention before the coder, or the scene reads primarily as a collection of product identities: remove or reduce the cameos; use zero if that remains unresolved.
The two visitors obscure the builder's action, fill the path's breathing room, or need enlargement and labels to be understood: remove them rather than making them another headline.
The illustration suggests official partnerships or ownership of the referenced products instead of optional tools/companions in Nag's scene: revise the framing; no unsupported affiliation claims.
